questions.q: How does data profiling differ from source analysis, as this lesson defines them?
options: They're the same activity under two different names
Profiling only applies after migration, never before
Source analysis is quantitative while profiling is purely subjective
Source analysis surveys the systems and their schema/access; profiling systematically measures the actual quality of the data inside them
questions.explain: Source analysis establishes what systems exist and how to access them. Profiling goes deeper, measuring the dataset against quality dimensions to turn vague worry into a quantified finding.

questions.q: A dataset has every required field populated, but 1,500 of its 10,000 records are duplicates of another record in the same file. Which data-quality dimension is clearly failing?
options: Completeness
Uniqueness
Validity
Accuracy
questions.explain: Completeness (fields populated) can score well while uniqueness (how many records represent the same real-world entity more than once) scores badly — they're independent dimensions, exactly as this lesson describes.

questions.q: What does Salesforce's standard Matching Rule for Contact compare, and how?
options: First Name and Last Name using fuzzy matching, together with Email using exact matching
Only Email, using fuzzy matching
Account Name using fuzzy matching, together with Billing Street and City using exact matching
Mailing address only, using exact matching
questions.explain: The standard Contact matching rule compares First Name and Last Name with fuzzy matching together with Email using exact matching. The Account rule (name + billing address fields) is a different standard rule entirely.

questions.q: What has to happen before Salesforce's standard Matching Rules do anything useful?
options: Nothing — they are active and enforcing duplicate blocking by default in every new org
They only work after a Duplicate Rule has already found at least one match manually
They have to be deliberately activated, since they ship inactive by default
They require a paid add-on before they can be turned on at all
questions.explain: Salesforce ships standard Matching Rules for Account, Contact, and Lead, but they are inactive by default and have to be deliberately turned on before they detect anything.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say a data-quality scorecard matters, beyond just producing numbers?
options: It satisfies a Salesforce platform requirement before any load can run
It replaces the need for source analysis entirely
It is only useful for audit purposes after the migration is already complete
It turns profiling findings into a concrete input that actually drives downstream decisions, like the scope conversation in the next lesson
questions.explain: Profiling only pays off if its output changes a downstream decision — the scorecard is what makes a finding like '60% uniqueness on Accounts' a concrete input to scope and later transformation design, rather than a number nobody acts on.
